text.p: Chrysler Corp. said Wednesday it extended its national consumer incentives programme, which offers cash allowances or reduced interest rate financing to buyers of some 1996 and 1997 models.
For most models, the programme is extended through July 7 from April 7.

Chrysler said the amounts of the cash allowances available under the programme are unchanged for all vehicles except the 1997 Dodge Ram Wagon, which qualifies for a $1,500 allowance as of April 1, up from $1,000 previously.

Instead of cash allowances, consumers can opt for lower annual percentage rate financing rates. The rate is 3.9 percent for loans of up to 60 months for the purchase of 1996 and 1997 Dodge Neon, Plymouth Neon, Dodge Avenger, Chrysler Sebring Coupe, Eagle Talon, Chrysler Cirrus, Dodge Stratus and Plymouth Breeze models.
The rate is 4.9 percent for loans of up to 60 months for the purchase of 1996 and 1997 Chrysler Concorde, Dodge Intrepid and Eagle Vision models.
Reduced financing rates on other vehicles in the programme are unchanged.
Chrysler's stock fell 37.5 cents to $30 on the New York Stock Exchange.
